How to get paid on time as a freelancer

Send reminders on a fixed schedule: three days after the due date, then ten days, then twenty.

Why a schedule works

A schedule takes the emotion out of chasing money. The client knows a reminder will come, and you never have to decide whether today is the day to send one. Most clients pay after the first or second reminder, because the invoice simply slipped down their inbox.

What to write

Keep each reminder short. Name the invoice number, the amount, the original due date and the payment link. Do not apologise for asking. The second reminder can add a firm date, and the third can mention a late fee if your contract allows one.

When to stop

After the third reminder, call the client or pause work until the invoice is paid. If that fails, a short letter that sets a final date often settles it without any further cost to you.
